contexts.api_surface: Implements core engine traits; search engine exposed via GET /search routes
contexts.description: Provides AI-powered data extraction and full-text search capabilities. engine-claude runs the Anthropic Claude CLI as a subprocess for LLM-driven field extraction with model/effort role routing; engine-wasm hosts untrusted WASM plugins under a CPU-fuel and memory cap via wasmtime; engine-search wraps an embedded tantivy index for faceted full-text search with entity enrichment and GC.
contexts.name: ai-extraction-engines

contexts.api_surface: GET /datasets, GET /datasets/:app, GET /query, GET /search, GET /provenance, GET /retention/preview, GET/POST /recipes, GET /remote
contexts.description: Axum route handlers for reading scraped data: list and fetch dataset rows with pagination; query derived columns; full-text search across indexed records; provenance tracing (which job produced a row); data retention management; saved recipes (parameterised query templates); and remote dataset proxy. This is the primary read path for consumers of scraped data.
contexts.name: api-data-access

contexts.api_surface: POST /jobs, GET /jobs, DELETE /jobs/:id, GET/POST/DELETE /schedules, POST /ingress, GET /receipt/:id, POST/GET /runtime
contexts.description: Axum route handlers for job lifecycle: enqueue, list, fetch, cancel jobs; manage cron schedules; handle ingress (bulk enqueue from external push); issue and verify job receipts; and control runtime state (pause/resume). Also ships two maintenance binaries: reindex (rebuilds Tantivy from SQLite) and search-backfill (populates derived search columns).
contexts.name: api-job-management

contexts.api_surface: GET /health, GET /datasets/doctor, GET /economics, GET /openapi.json, GET /host-weather, GET /events (SSE), GET/POST/DELETE /triggers, GET/POST/DELETE /watches, POST /provisioner
contexts.description: Axum route handlers for platform operations and automation: health-check, store doctor, cost economics, OpenAPI meta, host-weather conditions, SSE event stream, provisioner lifecycle, trigger management, and watch subscriptions. These routes span observability, governance, and the automation layer that consumers use to react to scraping events.
contexts.name: api-platform-ops

contexts.api_surface: MCP tool server endpoints; all routes wired here but defined in routes/
contexts.description: Server bootstrap and shared runtime state: main.rs wires all axum routers, middleware (HMAC auth, body-limit, Sentry), and graceful shutdown; state.rs holds the shared AppState injected into every handler; registry.rs maps app names to ScrapeApp impls; activity.rs and progress.rs emit SSE progress events; maintenance.rs runs periodic housekeeping; mcp/ exposes the MCP (Model Context Protocol) tool server for agent access.
contexts.name: api-server-core

contexts.api_surface: Registered as ScrapeApps; invoked via POST /jobs
contexts.description: Scrapes and structures US economic statistics from Census Bureau and federal sources: census-bfs (Business Formation Statistics), census-common (shared Census API helpers and row models), census-density (population density by county), census-nesd (non-employer statistics), census-nonemp (nonemployment demographics), trade-wages (BLS occupational wage data), trades-common (shared parsing for trades/occupation data), and cms-fee-schedule (CMS Medicare physician fee schedule). These apps feed a unified economic intelligence dataset.
contexts.name: census-economic-data

contexts.description: Implements the automated quality gates that block CI on flaky tests, oversized build caches, and lane-certification regressions. Each gate runs as a Node.js script, emits a structured verdict (0 clean / 2 findings / 3 cannot-check), and is exercised by a paired test file using node:test. The disk-check gate is self-healing — it prunes before measuring — while flake-check maintains a quarantine register with expiry and ceiling enforcement.
contexts.name: ci-quality-gates

contexts.api_surface: Each registered as ScrapeApp; invoked via POST /jobs
contexts.description: A suite of apps that monitor and aggregate content from external sources: hackernews (HN stories/comments), research (Claude-assisted research compilation with caching), readable (readability-extracted article text), watch (monitors a URL for content changes using simhash), connector-api-watch (monitors a connector API endpoint for schema changes), peer (mirrors datasets from a peer Pumper instance), provisioner (bootstraps a fresh Pumper deployment), and plugin (runs arbitrary WASM scraping plugins with observatory telemetry).
contexts.name: content-monitoring

contexts.api_surface: Internal Datasets API; exposed via /datasets routes
contexts.description: Detects whether a newly scraped page or dataset differs meaningfully from its previous version, preventing redundant downstream processing. Uses simhash (bitwise fingerprinting) to compare DOM trees, and the Datasets module to persist named row-keyed datasets with bulk upsert and batch-equivalence semantics. Drives the watch and trigger pipelines by emitting change events.
contexts.name: core-change-detection

contexts.api_surface: No HTTP surface; consumed by every app and engine crate
contexts.description: Defines the ScrapeApp and engine traits that every scraping app and engine must implement, plus the runtime config, tiered Fetcher (choosing the right engine per request), rate Governor, and host-profile memory. This is the dependency inversion seam that keeps apps independent of concrete engine crates; changing the engine a request uses is a config change, not a code change.
contexts.name: core-engine-contract

contexts.api_surface: No HTTP surface; consumed by every app crate
contexts.description: HTML/text extraction primitives shared by all scraping apps: CSS/XPath selectors via scraper, Markdown serialisation, LLM-guided field induction (induce.rs), and JSON salvage for partially-malformed LLM outputs. These utilities sit below the app layer and are the building blocks apps compose to turn raw HTML into structured records.
contexts.name: core-extraction

contexts.api_surface: No direct HTTP surface; used internally by engine-http and engine-claude
contexts.description: HTTP response cache backed by SQLite: stores raw response bodies keyed by URL hash with TTL eviction, an LRU in-memory layer, and VCR record/replay for deterministic testing. backup.rs provides SQLite WAL checkpoint and file-copy utilities for point-in-time snapshots. Together these enable offline test replay without live network access.
contexts.name: core-http-cache

contexts.api_surface: Internal Storage trait; exposed externally via /jobs routes
contexts.description: SQLite-backed durable job queue: enqueue, claim, heartbeat, complete/fail, and requeue semantics with idempotency keys, cause tracking, and per-job budget floors. Storage is the central write path for every scrape job; store_instrument wraps it with tracing chokepoints; jitter adds randomised delays to prevent thundering herds.
contexts.name: core-job-queue

contexts.api_surface: Catalog data read from catalog/data-sources.toml; no direct HTTP surface
contexts.description: Cross-cutting services that wire the platform together: catalog.rs is the machine-readable pipeline registry reader; costs.rs tracks per-job LLM token spend; recipes.rs manages saved API query templates with strike counting; plugin.rs is the WASM plugin host contract; process_env.rs, testing.rs, and search.rs provide test harness, process-level env access, and the search index interface. These are the services every other core module can depend on without creating circular deps.
contexts.name: core-platform-services

contexts.api_surface: GET /datasets/doctor, GET /retention/preview, GET /enforcement/preview
contexts.description: Detects degraded scraping performance (rate-limits, error spikes, yield collapses) and enforces circuit-breaker policies per app. The resilience module maintains rolling-window counters (sketch), persists enforcement state, previews what enforcement would do, and exposes an invariant-check surface. doctor.rs aggregates store health; retention.rs ages out old dataset rows.
contexts.name: core-resilience

contexts.api_surface: No HTTP surface; applied via sqlx::migrate at server startup
contexts.description: SQLite schema evolution for the entire Pumper data store: 43 sequential migrations covering jobs, datasets, simhash, watches, webhooks, triggers, schedules, cost ledger, resilience, provenance, and DataHub governance tables. Applied at startup via sqlx migrate; the migration history is the authoritative record of every table's lifecycle.
contexts.name: core-schema-migrations

contexts.api_surface: GET /datasets/doctor, GET /retention/preview, GET /enforcement/preview, GET /openapi.json (smoke-tested)
contexts.description: Enforces documentation-sync discipline and provides operational smoke-testing for the running server. The doc-sync hook (check-doc-sync.mjs) scans session transcripts for feature-source edits without matching docs/features updates and exits 2 as a reminder; its fixture suite validates the hook against representative transcript scenarios. smoke.ps1 boots the real server binary against a scratch config, drives an end-to-end job, and curl-checks key API surfaces, while disk-schedule.ps1 registers a weekly prune as a Windows scheduled task.
contexts.name: docs-and-ops-scripts

contexts.api_surface: Exercises /jobs, /ingress, error routes against live server
contexts.description: End-to-end tests that verify the HTTP API contract: error response shapes, enqueue/door parity, ingress gate behaviour, body-size limits, budget-terminal conditions, request panic containment, and router correctness. These tests exercise the API surface from the outside and guard against behavioural regressions in the request/response contract.
contexts.name: e2e-api-contract

contexts.api_surface: Exercises /datasets, /search, /jobs endpoints against live server
contexts.description: End-to-end tests that verify the integrity of the data pipeline: correct dataset reads after writes, delete-gate enforcement preventing partial deletes, engine conformance to the fetch contract, VCR playback accuracy, target-exclusion filtering, search degraded-mode behaviour, and dynamic app registration. These tests run the real server binary against a scratch store.
contexts.name: e2e-data-integrity

contexts.api_surface: Exercises full server stack; MCP tool server via mcp_live
contexts.description: End-to-end integration tests covering cross-system scenarios: the shared test harness, MCP tool server (both unit-level and live), MPSV app pipeline, peer-mirror replication, provisioner lifecycle, app-fetch chokepoints, and HTTP fetch proxy behaviour. These tests wire multiple subsystems together and are the highest-fidelity signal of end-to-end correctness.
contexts.name: e2e-integration

contexts.api_surface: Registered as ScrapeApps; invoked via POST /jobs with app=grants-gov, ca-grants, eu-sedia, cordis
contexts.description: Scrapes and structures funding opportunity data from multiple grant registries: grants-common provides shared parsing primitives, eligibility models, and dataset schemas used by all grant apps; grants-gov covers the US federal Grants.gov opportunity search and detail pipeline; ca-grants covers California state grants; eu-sedia scrapes EU SEDIA innovation funding; cordis indexes EU Horizon/CORDIS project data. Together they form a unified grants intelligence pipeline across US federal, US state, and EU sources.
contexts.name: grants-intelligence

contexts.api_surface: Consumes GET/POST/DELETE /schedules; no direct surface
contexts.description: Cron-based job scheduler that fires scrape jobs on user-defined schedules: evaluates cron expressions, enforces schedule budgets and overlap protection, tracks misfires, skips, and maturity windows, and re-enqueues jobs into the durable queue. The e2e tests verify scheduling truth (jobs fire when expected), budget enforcement, misfire handling, and overlap guards.
contexts.name: job-scheduler

contexts.api_surface: GET/POST/DELETE /triggers; triggers fire asynchronously after job completion
contexts.description: Event-driven trigger system: evaluates trigger conditions after each job completes, fires downstream jobs, manages trigger hop chains, runs WASM plugin hooks at each trigger stage, and maintains a trigger run ledger. E2e tests verify caching, multi-hop chains, plugin hook execution, requeue policies, and job-control honesty under trigger-driven conditions.
contexts.name: job-triggers-pipeline

contexts.api_surface: No direct HTTP surface; driven by the job queue
contexts.description: Worker pool that claims jobs from the SQLite queue and dispatches them to registered ScrapeApp implementations: manages concurrency limits, heartbeat keepalive, panic containment, and graceful drain on shutdown. fanout.rs fans one job out to multiple target sub-jobs; refresher.rs re-checks timed-out jobs. E2e tests cover lifecycle, fanout off-slot, drain, and memory reset.
contexts.name: job-worker

contexts.api_surface: Registered as ScrapeApps; invoked via POST /jobs
contexts.description: Scrapes pricing, valuation, and labour market data from commercial and government sources: state-tax (US state tax rates with derived join view), state-licensing (state occupational licensing requirements), homewyse-pricing (home improvement cost benchmarks), valuation-multiples (business valuation multiples by sector), transact (transaction/deal data), smlouvy-dump-watch (Czech public contracts registry dump watcher), mpsv-ispv (Czech MPSV wage statistics), and mpsv-vpm (Czech MPSV vacancy and employment portal).
contexts.name: pricing-valuation

contexts.api_surface: Consumes GET /datasets/{app}/{name}/export (NDJSON snapshot) and GET /datasets/{app}/{name}/changes (keyset-paged change feed)
contexts.description: The `@pumper/sync` TypeScript package gives downstream products a typed, incremental mirror of Pumper's canonical datasets. It exposes a stateless `PumperClient` for one-off reads (snapshot export, change-feed pages) and a higher-level `createPumperSync` watermark loop that keeps a consumer store up to date without re-fetching unchanged rows. The package has no runtime dependencies — only TypeScript and Node ≥ 20 — and ships as ESM with bundled type declarations.
contexts.name: pumper-sync-sdk

contexts.api_surface: WASM exports: alloc(len)->ptr, extract(ptr,len)->u64 (legacy), extract_v2(ptr,len)->u64, describe()->u64
contexts.description: Example WASM plugin crates that implement the pumper-engine-wasm host ABI (`alloc` / `extract_v2` / `describe`), compiled to `wasm32-unknown-unknown`. Covers two plugin kinds: extraction plugins (title-extractor pulls HTML title/h1; busyloop is a hostile fuel-budget fixture that never returns) and trigger-hook plugins (trigger-gate is a dataset predicate that gates trigger firing by count/dataset; delta-slim is a transform that slims the `_trigger` payload to a declared key list). Each crate is a standalone Cargo package; the justfile `just plugins-install` builds and installs the two production hooks into `data/plugins/`.
contexts.name: wasm-plugins

contexts.api_surface: Registered as ScrapeApp; invoked via POST /jobs with app=crawl or app=extractor
contexts.description: Provides general-purpose web crawling and LLM-assisted data extraction. crawl/ traverses link graphs with reliability tracking and produces structured telemetry; extractor/ uses Claude to extract structured records from HTML pages via configurable schemas, supporting source, replay, and induce modes with full provenance. These are the most general scraping building blocks above the engine layer.
contexts.name: web-crawl-extraction

contexts.api_surface: Implements core Fetcher + engine traits; no HTTP surface of its own
contexts.description: Provides HTTP fetch, headless browser rendering, web archive retrieval, and remote proxy fetch capabilities. Each engine implements the core Fetcher/engine trait so the server can swap transport strategies without changing app code. engine-http uses reqwest with retry budgets and rate limiting; engine-browser wraps chromiumoxide for JavaScript-rendered pages; engine-archive fetches from the Wayback Machine; engine-remote delegates to a remote Pumper instance.
contexts.name: web-scraping-engines

contexts.api_surface: GET /events (SSE); POST webhooks fired to external URLs; GET /datahub/governance/preview
contexts.description: Outbound webhook delivery with HMAC signing, retry backoff, and at-least-once semantics; SSE event fan-out for real-time browser/client subscriptions; and DataHub governance integration that polls dataset changes and applies governance-level actions. These three systems share the event-emission pipeline that notifies external systems of scraping outcomes.
contexts.name: webhook-event-delivery
